extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers and Scientific Review Officers (members of Scientific Review Groups)
extracted.subtask_short: NIH peer review of grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for NIH reviewers on evaluating grant applications, participating in study section meetings, scoring, writing critiques, and meeting integrity/conflict-of-interest requirements. Covers reviewer responsibilities and the tools/processes used (eRA/IAR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: First level peer reviewers assess the overall impact that a proposed project will likely have on the biomedical research field; the application’s final rating or ‘overall impact score’ is determined by the entire review panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how the project, if successful, will influence the field. Assigned reviewers provide preliminary evaluations, but the Scientific Review Group (SRG) discussion and full panel determine the final overall impact score. See 'Scoring in First Level Peer Review' and related scoring resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate using criteria established in the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must evaluate applications using the criteria established in the notice of funding opportunity to which an application(s) was submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the NOFO-specific review criteria; consult standard reviewer guidance documents for additional detail about how to evaluate each NOFO criterion. Links provided: 'Peer Review Criteria and Considerations', 'Review Criteria Information'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Criteria and Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional guidance for how to evaluate individual criteria is available through standard reviewer guidance documents (e.g., Peer Review Criteria and Considerations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the consolidated reviewer documents and the 'Peer Review Criteria and Considerations' materials to interpret and apply criterion-specific standards (for example, the typical NIH criteria such as significance, investigators, innovation, approach, environment when applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring (preliminary ratings and final scores)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are typically given a preliminary rating as part of assigned reviewers’ initial evaluations; however an application’s final rating or ‘overall impact score’ is determined by the entire review panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigned reviewers submit preliminary scores; the SRG discusses applications and the full panel submits final scores. Consult 'Scoring in First Level Peer Review' and consolidated scoring guidance for procedures and interpretation of scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing critiques and preparing the summary statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer critiques are part of the summary statement and an important source of feedback for what reviewers liked and didn’t like about an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare clear, constructive critiques that will appear in the summary statement. Use IAR to submit and manage critiques; reviewers can view other reviewers’ critiques. See 'Reviewer Critique Information' for expectations and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity, Confidentiality, and Conflicts of Interest (COI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are required to certify that they understand the rules of integrity and confidentiality in the peer review process and the consequences for not following these rules. They must also certify before and after review meetings that all conflicts of interest were identified and declared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete required certifications in IAR (pre-meeting and post-meeting COI). Undertake mandated trainings in review integrity and bias awareness to participate in most NIH review meetings. See 'Integrity and Confidentiality in NIH Peer Review', 'Managing Conflicts of Interest in NIH Peer Review', and 'Review Integrity and Bias Awareness Training'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects, vertebrate animals, and biohazard considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of the meeting, the SRG will discuss any concerns with the use of human subjects, vertebrate animals, and/or biohazards within applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and discuss protections, ethical issues, and regulatory compliance for human subjects and animal use; consider these concerns in impact assessment and scoring. Consult policy-specific reviewer guidance where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review meetings and roles (Scientific Review Group participation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are brought together as a Scientific Review Group (SRG) to discuss the merits of the studies proposed in individual applications and submit a final impact score for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand meeting roles and procedures (e.g., assigned reviewers, discussants, chair). Participate in SRG discussion, attend mock study sections if helpful, and follow meeting overview materials to learn how reviewers discuss applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet Assisted Review (IAR) responsibilities and workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: IAR is the eRA web-based module used by reviewers to view meeting materials, certify confidentiality and COI forms, access applications, and submit scores and critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use IAR to: access meeting materials; fill out personal profile; certify pre-meeting COI; submit and manage critiques and scores; view other reviewers’ critiques; submit final scores; certify post-meeting COI. Consult 'IAR for Reviewers Online Help' and 'For Reviewers: Navigating IAR' for step-by-step instructions.
